assertions: Phase 4 utterance evidence remains immutable and is verified by complete canonical digest.
The closed versioned vocabulary assigns every one of 145 act types to exactly one of thirteen families.
Multiple compatible acts may be selected without forcing a dominant label.
Unknown and explicitly unclassified utterances are valid outcomes.
Every selected act retains exact Phase 4 text-view, character-offset, word, source-interval, and confidence evidence.
Identified, probable, multiple-candidate, implicit, and unresolved targets remain distinct.
Provider proposals cannot become authoritative without normalization, validation, and selection.
Act, span, target, selection, question, answer, quotation, and procedural confidence remain distinct dimensions.
Canonical acts retain observation and candidate provenance.
Correction propagation invalidates affected spans and preserves justified unaffected identifiers.
Strict persistence is sealed, reloadable, and refuses source or evidence mismatch.
Assertion does not imply truth, answer adequacy, rebuttal success, procedural violation, intent, or participant merit.
limitations: This slice qualifies contract, lineage, addressing, selection, and provider-boundary mechanics rather than discourse classification accuracy.
Deterministic classification and domain-specific relation artifacts begin in later slices.
